What can be built? Height & units by subdistrict

Hilliard Chapter 1116 Community Development Districts — draft dated Oct. 27, 2026 (pages stamped "DRAFT 10-02-2026"). Covers the three districts mapped in this draft: Downtown Hilliard (D), Gateway (G) and Heritage Trail (H).

How the numbers work. Heights, story counts and building width/depth limits come from the Height & Massing tables in §1116.09–.11. The draft sets no units-per-acre cap; density is controlled by which building typologies are allowed and by the building envelope. "Units per building" reflects the largest residential typology allowed: Quadraplex (4) in D-4, 4-8 Unit Building (8) in G-4, and Multi-Unit Building (8+, no maximum) elsewhere. Actual unit counts in those subdistricts depend on the building envelope, parking and site conditions.

FAR (floor-area ratio). Max building coverage × max stories, from each district's Lot Development and Height & Massing tables: the most floor area a lot could hold relative to its size. It is a regulatory ceiling; parking, setbacks, open space and the 50-ft adjacency setback will lower what is achievable. The D-5 figure is lower (2.85) for buildings fronting Main Street, which are capped at 3 stories.

3D view. Each subdistrict is raised to its maximum principal building height, exaggerated 3× vertically so the differences read at city scale. It shows the allowed envelope, not expected buildout.

Map accuracy. District boundaries were digitized from the draft's own district maps (§1116.09–.11) and fitted to street centerlines; expect errors of roughly 10–30 m. The gray base map is those same draft maps. Typology photos are from §1116.03, which labels them illustrative, not regulatory. The Big Darby Employment and I-270 Corridor districts are not mapped in this draft and are not shown.
